events.text: God creates light and separates it from darkness.
God forms the sky, land, seas, and plants.
God places the sun, moon, and stars in the heavens.
God fills the sea and sky with living creatures, then land animals.
God creates man and woman in His own image.
God rests on the seventh day and blesses it.

stories.title: Adam and Eve in the Garden

events.text: God places Adam in the Garden of Eden to tend it.
God forms Eve from Adam's rib to be his companion.
A serpent tempts Eve to eat fruit from the forbidden tree.
Adam and Eve eat the fruit and realize they are naked.
God confronts them, and they are sent out of the garden.
God tells Abram to leave his country and his father's house.
God promises to make Abram into a great nation.
Abram takes his wife Sarai and his nephew Lot and departs.
They travel through Canaan, and Abram builds altars to the LORD.

stories.title: The Promise of a Son to Abraham and Sarah

events.text: Three visitors come to Abraham's tent in the heat of the day.
They promise that Sarah will have a son within the year.
Sarah, listening at the tent door, laughs in disbelief.
The LORD asks, "Is any thing too hard for the LORD?"
In time, Sarah gives birth to Isaac, just as promised.

stories.title: Hagar and Ishmael in the Wilderness

events.text: Sarah sends Hagar and her son Ishmael away into the wilderness.
Their water runs out, and Hagar despairs for her son's life.
An angel of God calls to Hagar from heaven.
God opens her eyes, and she sees a well of water.
God is with Ishmael as he grows up in the wilderness.

stories.title: The Destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah

events.text: Two angels come to Sodom and are welcomed by Lot.
The angels warn Lot to flee the city with his family.
Lot, his wife, and daughters escape as fire and brimstone fall.
Lot's wife looks back and becomes a pillar of salt.
Abraham sends his servant to find a wife for Isaac.
The servant prays for a sign at a well outside the city.
Rebekah offers water to the servant and his camels, fulfilling the sign.
Rebekah agrees to travel back with the servant to marry Isaac.
Isaac loves Rebekah, and she becomes his wife.
Jacob flees from his brother Esau and stops to sleep at Bethel.
He dreams of a ladder reaching from earth to heaven, with angels on it.
The LORD stands above it and renews His promise to Jacob.
Jacob wakes in awe and sets up a stone as a pillar to mark the place.

stories.title: Jacob's Marriages to Rachel and Leah

events.text: Jacob meets Rachel at a well and falls in love with her.
He agrees to work seven years for Laban to marry Rachel.
Laban deceives Jacob, giving him Leah instead on the wedding night.
Jacob works seven more years and finally marries Rachel too.
Pharaoh has troubling dreams that none of his wise men can explain.
Joseph is brought from prison to interpret the dreams.
Joseph explains that seven years of plenty will be followed by seven years of famine.
Pharaoh sets Joseph over all the land of Egypt to prepare for the famine.

stories.title: Joseph Reveals Himself to His Brothers

events.text: Joseph's brothers come to Egypt to buy grain during the famine.
Joseph tests his brothers, hiding his identity at first.
Unable to hold back any longer, Joseph reveals who he is.
Joseph forgives his brothers and weeps with them.
Joseph sends for his father Jacob to come to Egypt.
God speaks to Jacob in a vision, telling him not to fear going to Egypt.
Jacob's whole family travels down to Egypt to be with Joseph.
Pharaoh gives them the land of Goshen to settle in.
Pharaoh orders that every Hebrew baby boy be thrown into the Nile.
Moses' mother hides him for three months, then places him in a basket on the river.
Pharaoh's daughter finds the basket and adopts Moses as her own.
Moses' own mother is hired to nurse him as a baby.
Moses sees an Egyptian beating a Hebrew slave and kills the Egyptian.
Fearing Pharaoh, Moses flees to the land of Midian.
Moses helps the daughters of a priest water their flocks at a well.
Moses marries Zipporah and becomes a shepherd in Midian.
God sends Moses and Aaron to demand Pharaoh let Israel go.
Pharaoh refuses and makes the Israelites' labor even harder.
Moses returns again and again as each plague strikes Egypt.
After the tenth plague, Pharaoh finally lets Israel go.
God instructs each Israelite family to select a lamb without blemish.
They mark their doorposts with the lamb's blood.
The angel of death passes over the marked houses that night.
Israel eats the meal in haste, ready to leave Egypt.

stories.title: The Ten Commandments Given at Sinai

events.text: Israel camps at the foot of Mount Sinai.
God calls Moses up the mountain amid thunder, lightning, and smoke.
God gives Moses the Ten Commandments written on stone tablets.
Moses comes down the mountain to teach the people God's law.
The leader of each tribe brings a rod to be placed before the LORD.
Aaron's rod, representing the tribe of Levi, is placed among them.
Overnight, Aaron's rod buds, blossoms, and produces almonds.
The budded rod confirms Aaron as God's chosen priest.

stories.title: The Bronze Serpent in the Wilderness

events.text: The people grow impatient and speak against God and Moses.
The LORD sends venomous snakes among the people.
The people confess their sin and ask Moses to pray for them.
God tells Moses to make a bronze serpent, and all who look upon it live.
King Balak hires the prophet Balaam to curse Israel.
On the way, Balaam's donkey sees an angel blocking the road and refuses to move.
The LORD opens the donkey's mouth, and it speaks to Balaam.
Balaam's eyes are opened to see the angel, and he blesses Israel instead of cursing them.
Korah and his followers rise up against Moses' leadership.
Moses tells the people to separate themselves from Korah's tents.
The ground opens beneath Korah and his household, swallowing them.
The rest of Israel sees and fears the LORD's judgment.

stories.title: The Twelve Spies and Israel's Unbelief

events.text: Moses sends twelve spies to explore the land of Canaan.
Ten spies bring back a fearful report of giants in the land.
Joshua and Caleb alone urge the people to trust God and go in.
Because of their unbelief, Israel wanders in the wilderness forty years.
God tells Moses to climb Mount Nebo to view the Promised Land.
The LORD shows Moses the whole land from the mountaintop.
Moses dies there at the age of a hundred and twenty.
The LORD buries him, and no one knows the place of his grave.

stories.title: Crossing the Jordan River into Canaan

events.text: Joshua leads Israel to the edge of the flooded Jordan River.
The priests carrying the Ark of the Covenant step into the water.
The water stops flowing, and the riverbed dries up before them.
All Israel crosses over on dry ground into the Promised Land.
Twelve stones are set up at Gilgal to remember the crossing.
Naomi loses her husband and both sons while living in Moab.
Ruth chooses to stay with Naomi rather than return to her own people.
Ruth gleans grain in the field of Boaz, a relative of Naomi's husband.
Boaz marries Ruth, and she becomes the great-grandmother of King David.
An angel calls Gideon to deliver Israel from the Midianites.
Gideon asks for a sign, laying out a fleece of wool overnight.
The fleece is wet with dew while the ground stays dry.
Gideon asks for the opposite sign, and God grants it too.
Samson, a Nazirite of great strength, falls in love with Delilah.
The Philistines bribe Delilah to discover the secret of his strength.
Delilah persuades Samson to reveal that his strength lies in his uncut hair.
His hair is cut while he sleeps, and the Philistines capture him.
Jonathan, Saul's son, becomes close friends with David.
Jonathan gives David his robe, armor, and weapons as a sign of covenant.
Jonathan warns David of Saul's growing jealousy and plans to kill him.
The two friends part in sorrow, promising loyalty to each other's families.
Saul pursues David with an army into the wilderness.
Saul enters a cave to rest, not knowing David is hiding inside.
David secretly cuts off a corner of Saul's robe instead of killing him.
David shows Saul the piece of robe, proving he means no harm.
David sees Bathsheba bathing and sends for her.
David arranges for her husband Uriah to be killed in battle.
The prophet Nathan confronts David with a parable exposing his sin.
David repents deeply, and God forgives him though consequences remain.
Absalom, David's son, wins the hearts of the people and declares himself king.
David flees Jerusalem to escape his son's rebellion.
In battle, Absalom's hair catches in a tree, and Joab kills him.
David mourns deeply for his rebellious son.
Solomon dies, and his son Rehoboam becomes king.
The people ask Rehoboam to lighten Solomon's heavy burdens.
Rehoboam follows harsh advice and threatens to rule even more severely.
Ten tribes rebel and follow Jeroboam, splitting the kingdom in two.

stories.title: The Queen of Sheba Visits Solomon

events.text: The Queen of Sheba hears of Solomon's great wisdom and wealth.
She travels a great distance to test him with hard questions.
Solomon answers all her questions, and she sees his wisdom firsthand.
She praises the God of Israel and gives Solomon many gifts.
Nehemiah hears that Jerusalem's walls lie broken and burned.
He asks the king for permission to return and rebuild them.
Despite mockery and threats from enemies, the people work together.
The wall is completed in just fifty-two days.
A great army comes against King Jehoshaphat of Judah.
Jehoshaphat calls the nation to fast and seek the LORD.
He appoints singers to march ahead of the army, praising God.
As they sing, the enemy armies turn on each other and are destroyed.
King Hezekiah becomes deathly ill, and Isaiah tells him to prepare to die.
Hezekiah prays earnestly, weeping before the LORD.
God hears his prayer and promises fifteen more years of life.
As a sign, God moves the sun's shadow backward ten steps.
A widow cries out to Elisha because creditors want to take her sons as slaves.
Elisha asks what she has left, and she says only a small jar of oil.
He tells her to borrow many empty jars and pour her oil into them.
The oil miraculously fills every jar, and she sells it to pay her debts.

stories.title: Elisha and the Shunammite Woman's Son

events.text: A woman from Shunem prepares a room for Elisha whenever he passes through.
Elisha promises her that she will have a son, and she does.
Years later, the boy suddenly dies of a severe headache.
Elisha comes and stretches himself over the boy, and he comes back to life.
Naaman, a great commander, suffers from leprosy.
A servant girl tells him of a prophet in Israel who could heal him.
Elisha instructs Naaman to wash seven times in the Jordan River.
Naaman obeys, and his skin becomes clean like a child's.

stories.title: Elisha and the Floating Axe Head

events.text: A group of prophets is cutting timber by the Jordan River.
One man's borrowed axe head falls into the water and sinks.
Elisha throws a stick into the water at the spot.
The iron axe head floats to the surface.
Queen Jezebel threatens Elijah's life after his victory on Mount Carmel.
Elijah flees into the wilderness, exhausted and afraid.
An angel feeds him, and he travels forty days to Mount Horeb.
God speaks to Elijah not in wind or fire, but in a still small voice.
God tells Elijah to find Elisha and anoint him as his successor.
Elijah finds Elisha plowing a field with oxen.
Elijah throws his mantle over Elisha's shoulders.
Elisha leaves his oxen behind and follows Elijah to serve him.

stories.title: Micaiah's True Prophecy Against False Prophets

events.text: King Ahab gathers four hundred prophets who promise him victory in battle.
King Jehoshaphat asks if there is a true prophet of the LORD to consult.
Micaiah is brought in and, unlike the others, prophesies Ahab's defeat.
Ahab ignores the warning, goes to battle, and is killed as Micaiah foretold.
Jeremiah's warnings to surrender to Babylon anger the king's officials.
They lower Jeremiah into a muddy, empty cistern to silence him.
Ebed-melech, a royal official, pleads with the king for Jeremiah's life.
Jeremiah is pulled out of the cistern with ropes and rags.
God tells Jeremiah to go down to the potter's house.
Jeremiah watches the potter reshape a marred piece of clay on the wheel.
The LORD explains that He can reshape Israel just as the potter reshapes the clay.
Jeremiah delivers this message of warning and hope to the people.
God shows Ezekiel a scroll filled with words of lamentation and woe.
God commands Ezekiel to eat the scroll before speaking to Israel.
Ezekiel eats it, and it tastes as sweet as honey in his mouth.
He is sent to speak God's words to a rebellious nation.
God tells Hosea to marry Gomer, a woman who would be unfaithful.
Gomer leaves Hosea and falls into hardship and slavery.
God tells Hosea to buy her back and love her again.
Hosea's redeeming love pictures God's faithful love for unfaithful Israel.
Amos, a shepherd called to prophesy, receives a vision from God.
The LORD stands beside a wall holding a plumbline.
God explains that He is measuring Israel against His standard of justice.
Amos warns that Israel has failed to measure up and judgment is coming.
Habakkuk questions God about why evil goes unpunished in Judah.
God answers that He is raising up the Chaldeans to bring judgment.
Habakkuk climbs his watchtower to wait for the LORD's reply.
God assures him that the just shall live by faith, and Habakkuk responds with a song of trust.
A woman has ten silver coins and loses one of them.
She lights a lamp and sweeps the house carefully to search for it.
She searches diligently until she finds the lost coin.
She calls her friends and neighbors together to rejoice with her.

stories.title: The Parable of the Two Sons

events.text: A father asks his first son to go work in the vineyard.
The first son refuses at first, but later changes his mind and goes.
The father asks his second son the same, and he agrees but never goes.
Jesus asks which son truly did his father's will.

stories.title: The Persistent Widow and the Judge

events.text: A widow repeatedly comes to an unjust judge seeking justice.
The judge, who fears neither God nor man, keeps refusing her.
Because she keeps bothering him, he finally grants her request.
Jesus teaches that God will surely answer His people who cry out to Him.

stories.title: The Pharisee and the Tax Collector

events.text: Two men go up to the temple to pray.
The Pharisee prays proudly, thanking God he is not like other sinners.
The tax collector stands far off, beating his chest and asking for mercy.
Jesus says the humble tax collector, not the proud Pharisee, went home justified.
A rich man's land produces an abundant harvest.
He decides to tear down his barns and build bigger ones to store it all.
He tells himself to relax, eat, drink, and be merry for years to come.
God calls him a fool, for his life will be required of him that very night.
A rich man lives in luxury while a poor beggar named Lazarus lies at his gate.
Both men die; Lazarus is carried to Abraham's side, and the rich man is tormented.
The rich man begs for relief and for someone to warn his brothers.
Abraham explains that they already have Moses and the prophets to listen to.
A wise man builds his house on a foundation of solid rock.
A foolish man builds his house on sand instead.
Rain falls, floods rise, and winds beat against both houses.
The house on the rock stands firm, but the house on the sand collapses.

stories.title: The Parable of the Ten Virgins

events.text: Ten virgins take their lamps to wait for the bridegroom.
Five are wise and bring extra oil; five are foolish and do not.
The bridegroom is delayed, and all of them fall asleep.
At midnight the cry comes, and only those with enough oil are ready to enter.
A king forgives a servant an enormous debt he could never repay.
That same servant finds a fellow servant who owes him a small amount.
He refuses to forgive the small debt and has the man thrown in prison.
The king hears of this and hands the unforgiving servant over to be punished.
A landowner hires workers for his vineyard early in the morning.
He goes out again at various hours and hires more workers.
At the end of the day, he pays every worker the same generous wage.
Those hired first grumble, but the owner says he has been fair and generous.

stories.title: The Parable of the Mustard Seed

events.text: Jesus compares the kingdom of heaven to a tiny mustard seed.
A man plants the seed in his field.
Though it is the smallest of seeds, it grows into a large tree.
Birds of the air come and nest in its branches.
Jesus compares the kingdom of heaven to yeast.
A woman takes the yeast and mixes it into a large amount of flour.
The yeast works quietly and invisibly through the dough.
In time, the yeast leavens the entire batch.
A king prepares a wedding feast for his son and sends out invitations.
The invited guests make excuses and refuse to come.
The king sends his servants into the streets to invite anyone they find.
The wedding hall is filled with guests, both good and bad.

stories.title: The Parable of the Growing Seed

events.text: A man scatters seed on the ground.
He sleeps and rises night and day while the seed sprouts and grows.
He does not know exactly how it happens, but the earth produces grain by itself.
When the grain is ripe, he puts in the sickle to harvest it.
Jesus compares the kingdom of heaven to a net cast into the sea.
The net gathers fish of every kind.
When it is full, the fishermen pull it ashore.
They collect the good fish into baskets and throw the bad ones away.

stories.title: The Visit of the Wise Men

events.text: Wise men from the East see a star and follow it toward Jerusalem.
They ask King Herod where the newborn King of the Jews can be found.
The star leads them to the house where the young child Jesus is.
They worship Him and present gifts of gold, frankincense, and myrrh.
An angel warns Joseph in a dream that Herod seeks to kill the child.
Joseph takes Mary and Jesus and flees by night to Egypt.
Herod, enraged, orders the deaths of infant boys in Bethlehem.
After Herod dies, an angel tells Joseph it is safe to return.

stories.title: Jesus in the Temple at Age Twelve

events.text: Jesus' family travels to Jerusalem for the Passover feast.
On the journey home, Mary and Joseph realize Jesus is missing.
They find Him in the temple, sitting among the teachers, listening and asking questions.
Jesus returns home with them and grows in wisdom and favor.
The Spirit leads Jesus into the wilderness to fast for forty days.
The devil tempts Jesus to turn stones into bread.
The devil tempts Jesus to throw Himself from the temple.
The devil offers Jesus all the kingdoms of the world if He will worship him.
Jesus resists each temptation with Scripture, and the devil leaves Him.
Jesus sees Peter and Andrew casting their nets into the sea.
He calls out to them to follow Him and become fishers of men.
They immediately leave their nets and follow Him.
Jesus calls James and John, who leave their boat and father to follow too.
Jesus enters the temple and finds merchants and money changers there.
He is angered that His Father's house has become a marketplace.
He overturns their tables and drives them out.
He declares that the temple should be a house of prayer.

stories.title: Jesus and the Woman at the Well

events.text: Jesus stops to rest at a well in Samaria at midday.
A Samaritan woman comes to draw water, and Jesus asks her for a drink.
Jesus offers her living water and reveals He knows all about her life.
She believes He is the Christ and tells her whole town about Him.
Jesus sends disciples to bring a young donkey for Him to ride.
He rides into Jerusalem as crowds spread their cloaks on the road.
The people wave palm branches and shout, "Hosanna!"
Jesus enters the city, fulfilling the prophecy of a humble king.
During supper, Jesus rises and wraps a towel around His waist.
He pours water into a basin and begins washing His disciples' feet.
Peter protests, but Jesus explains the meaning of His humble act.
Jesus tells them to follow His example and serve one another.
Jesus prays in agony in the Garden of Gethsemane.
Judas arrives with soldiers and betrays Jesus with a kiss.
Peter draws a sword and cuts off a servant's ear, but Jesus heals him.
Jesus is arrested, and the disciples flee.
Peter follows at a distance as Jesus is taken to the high priest's house.
A servant girl recognizes Peter and says he was with Jesus.
Peter denies knowing Jesus three times before a rooster crows.
Peter remembers Jesus' words and weeps bitterly.

stories.title: Jesus Appears on the Road to Emmaus

events.text: Two disciples walk toward Emmaus, discussing Jesus' death in sorrow.
The risen Jesus joins them, but they do not recognize Him.
He explains from the Scriptures all that was written about Him.
When He breaks bread with them, their eyes are opened and they recognize Him.
Jesus gathers His disciples on a mountain near Bethany.
He commissions them to be His witnesses to the ends of the earth.
As they watch, He is lifted up and a cloud takes Him from their sight.
Two angels tell them Jesus will return in the same way He left.
Jesus and His disciples attend a wedding feast in Cana.
The wine runs out, and Mary tells Jesus of the need.
Jesus tells the servants to fill six stone jars with water.
The water becomes the finest wine, and the guests are amazed.
Peter and his companions have fished all night and caught nothing.
Jesus tells Peter to let down his nets one more time.
The nets fill with so many fish that they begin to break.
Peter falls at Jesus' feet, amazed and humbled.
A Roman centurion's servant lies sick and near death.
The centurion sends word asking Jesus to heal him.
He tells Jesus He need only speak the word, and it will be done.
Jesus marvels at his faith, and the servant is healed that same hour.

stories.title: Healing the Man with a Withered Hand

events.text: Jesus enters the synagogue on the Sabbath and sees a man with a withered hand.
Religious leaders watch to see if Jesus will heal on the Sabbath.
Jesus tells the man to stretch out his hand.
The man's hand is completely restored.

stories.title: Healing the Woman with the Issue of Blood

events.text: A woman who had bled for twelve years pushes through a crowd toward Jesus.
She touches the edge of His cloak, believing it will heal her.
She is instantly healed, and Jesus feels power go out from Him.
Jesus tells her that her faith has made her well.
Jairus, a synagogue leader, begs Jesus to heal his dying daughter.
Word comes that the girl has already died.
Jesus tells Jairus not to fear, only to believe.
Jesus takes her hand, and she rises, alive and well.

stories.title: Casting Out the Legion of Demons

events.text: Jesus meets a man possessed by many demons, living among the tombs.
The demons identify themselves as "Legion" and beg not to be sent away.
Jesus permits them to enter a herd of pigs nearby.
The herd rushes into the sea, and the man is found calm and in his right mind.
Ten men with leprosy call out to Jesus for mercy from a distance.
Jesus tells them to go show themselves to the priests.
As they go, all ten are cleansed of their leprosy.
Only one returns to thank Jesus, and Jesus notes the other nine did not.
Jesus sees a man who has been blind since birth.
He makes mud with spit and anoints the man's eyes.
He tells the man to wash in the Pool of Siloam.
The man washes and comes back seeing.
A great crowd has been with Jesus three days with nothing to eat.
The disciples find only seven loaves and a few small fish.
Jesus gives thanks, breaks the bread, and the disciples distribute it.
Everyone eats and is satisfied, with seven baskets of leftovers gathered.

stories.title: Healing the Deaf and Mute Man

events.text: People bring Jesus a man who is deaf and can hardly speak.
Jesus takes him aside privately from the crowd.
He touches the man's ears and tongue and says, "Be opened."
The man's ears are opened, and he speaks plainly.

stories.title: The Coin in the Fish's Mouth

events.text: Tax collectors ask Peter whether Jesus pays the temple tax.
Jesus tells Peter to go cast a hook into the sea.
He says the first fish caught will have a coin in its mouth.
Peter finds the coin exactly as Jesus said and pays the tax for them both.

stories.title: The Cursing of the Fig Tree

events.text: Jesus, hungry, approaches a fig tree full of leaves but no fruit.
He curses the tree, saying no one will eat fruit from it again.
The next day, the disciples find the tree withered from the roots.
Jesus uses the moment to teach them about faith and prayer.
A father brings his son, tormented by a spirit, to Jesus' disciples, but they cannot heal him.
The father brings the boy to Jesus and begs for help, if He is able.
Jesus rebukes the spirit, and it leaves the boy.
The disciples later ask privately why they could not cast it out, and Jesus speaks of prayer and faith.

stories.title: Healing at the Pool of Bethesda

events.text: A man who had been sick for thirty-eight years lies by the pool of Bethesda.
Jesus asks him if he wants to be made well.
The man explains he has no one to help him into the healing waters.
Jesus tells him to rise, take up his bed, and walk, and he is instantly healed.
Ananias and his wife Sapphira sell a piece of property.
They secretly keep back part of the money while claiming to give it all.
Peter confronts Ananias, who falls down dead upon hearing the truth exposed.
Sapphira arrives later, repeats the same lie, and also falls down dead.
Stephen, full of the Spirit, preaches boldly before the Jewish council.
He recounts Israel's history and accuses the council of resisting the Spirit.
Enraged, the council drags Stephen out of the city and stones him.
Stephen prays for his killers' forgiveness as he dies, becoming the first Christian martyr.
An angel sends Philip to a desert road, where he meets an Ethiopian official.
The official is reading from the prophet Isaiah but doesn't understand it.
Philip explains that the passage points to Jesus.
The official believes and asks to be baptized right there beside the road.
Peter falls into a trance while praying on a rooftop.
He sees a great sheet lowered from heaven, full of all kinds of animals.
A voice tells him to kill and eat, but Peter refuses, calling them unclean.
The voice tells him not to call unclean what God has made clean.
Cornelius, a devout Roman centurion, is told in a vision to send for Peter.
Peter, guided by his own vision, agrees to visit Cornelius's house.
Peter preaches the gospel to Cornelius and his household.
The Holy Spirit falls on them, and they are baptized as the first Gentile believers.
A dispute arises over whether Gentile believers must follow the law of Moses.
Paul and Barnabas travel to Jerusalem to discuss the matter with the apostles.
Peter and James speak, agreeing that salvation is by grace, not the law.
The council sends a letter freeing Gentile believers from that requirement.
The Holy Spirit sets apart Paul and Barnabas for a special work.
The church at Antioch fasts, prays, and sends them out.
They sail to Cyprus and then travel through Asia Minor preaching the gospel.
They appoint elders in every church they establish along the way.

stories.title: Paul at the Areopagus in Athens

events.text: Paul is troubled by the many idols he sees throughout Athens.
He is invited to speak before the philosophers at the Areopagus.
He references an altar "to the unknown god" to introduce the true God.
Some mock him, but others believe and follow him.
Paul's preaching turns many away from worshiping the goddess Diana.
A silversmith named Demetrius stirs up anger over lost business making idols.
A great crowd fills the theater, shouting in confusion for hours.
The city clerk calms the crowd and disperses them.
Paul preaches a very long sermon late into the night.
A young man named Eutychus, sitting in a window, falls asleep.
He falls three stories to the ground and is found dead.
Paul embraces him, and he is restored to life, to everyone's relief.

stories.title: Paul's Shipwreck on the Way to Rome

events.text: Paul, a prisoner, sails toward Rome to stand trial before Caesar.
A violent storm tosses the ship for many days.
An angel assures Paul that everyone aboard will survive.
The ship runs aground, and all passengers safely reach the island of Malta.

stories.title: Paul Bitten by a Viper on Malta

events.text: Paul gathers sticks to help build a fire for the shipwrecked survivors.
A viper, driven out by the heat, fastens itself on his hand.
The islanders expect Paul to swell up and die.
Paul shakes off the snake and suffers no harm, amazing everyone.

stories.title: Barnabas and Paul Sent Out from Antioch

events.text: The believers at Antioch are worshiping and fasting together.
The Holy Spirit says, "Separate me Barnabas and Saul for the work."
The church fasts, prays, and lays hands on them.
Barnabas and Paul are sent out to spread the gospel to new regions.

stories.title: The Choosing of the Seven Deacons

events.text: A dispute arises over the daily distribution of food to widows.
The apostles decide to appoint others to oversee this important work.
The church chooses seven men full of the Spirit and wisdom, including Stephen.
The apostles pray and lay hands on them, and the church continues to grow.

stories.title: James, Brother of John, Martyred by Herod

events.text: King Herod begins to persecute members of the church.
He arrests James, the brother of John, one of the twelve apostles.
Herod has James put to death with the sword.
Seeing this pleased some, Herod goes on to arrest Peter as well.
